chapter: Leaving home: Fisk, Tulsa, Arkansas City
title: Four Roses and his first bad experiences with liquor
summary: A non-drinker, he took a pint of Four Roses to a party and got sick; he recalls a similar first episode in high school and his father's mild advice.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, had you saved up some money now?
I'd saved up some money then.
Well, I'd like to know how your thinking was then. So by then, you'd been playing music for about a year, I guess, had you or more?
Right.
And you just -- you loved the life, I guess.

Well, I'll tell you the truth, I didn't drink a thing. People couldn't understand. They said, "I've never seen a musician that didn't drink." People would come in the clubs and would want to buy me a drink, you know, I just didn't drink and people didn't -- you know, they just couldn't understand it. So finally, I met some girl, you know, there in Arkansas City, and so-she told me, "I want to invite you to a party." She says, "But now, when you come to the party, the party will start about the time after you all get off from work. But when you come to the party, I want you to bring some whisky." Well, I don't know nothing about no whiskey, you know?

So I told the guy that night that I'm working for, Babe Burton, I says, "Look, I'm supposed to go to a party. They want me to bring some whiskey. What would you suggest?" He said, "Well, I got some Four Roses here." And that sounded good to me, Four Roses. Oh, I said, "Four Roses?"
Always sounds good.
(Laughter.)
I thought, "Well, that's what I want."

So he gave me, I guess it might have been a pint of Four Roses. So I'm a big man tonight, you know. Big man. They come by and pick me up and, "Girls, we've got Four Roses tonight. This is Four Roses. Don't forget. This is Four Roses." Oh, boy. Everybody else was older than I was. They were more experienced, you know, and I guess they could tell. They said, "Well, we got a jay hawk here, you know what I mean."
But anyway, everybody -- nobody got high but me.
(Laughter.)

Sick, you know. So that was sort of my first to getting exposed to the booze, you know, and of course, I had gotten exposed earlier in my high school year at one time, because I played for a party for some lawyer and I even rode my bicycle to the gig and after the gig, came home.
(Laughter.)
I couldn't even put the bicycle on the porch, I was so, you know. But when I came in the house, I came in and I just got deathly sick and laid across the bed and everything came up, you know.
What had you been drinking then?

I think they gave me a little booze that night. It didn't have to be much because, you know, I didn't know anything about it. And so I heard my mother tell my dad, she says, "You know, I smell whiskey." He said, "Oh,
it's somebody in the neighborhood making it." She said, "No, this smells like it's coming from that boy's room."
(Laughter.)
He says, "Oh, go on back to sleep now. That's some of the bootleggers in the neighborhood." She says, "Well, I'm going to get up and look."
(Laughter.)
She got up and turned the light on. She said, "Oh, my goodness. Look what this devil has done."
(Laughter.)

She says, "Oh, get up right now. Get up, get out of this bed and clean this up." Oh, I was so sick. She made me get up and clean it up. So I figured, I said, "Well, I know it's going to be something else tomorrow." "I'm going to have your daddy to get on you. I'm going to have him to skin you alive."

So the next day, the old man told me, "Come here, boy. Listen, now, you go to these places here. You tell them to give you something like punch. Don't give you none of that other stuff." I said, "Okay, that's what I'll do." So that was the end of that. That's all he ever said to me, you know?
: Were you drinking it straight or what were you doing?
Well, they had it mixed, but you know, when you have never had that stuff, it hits your stomach and
